status: provisional; adjust weights based on accepted data and held-out evaluation
description: One proposal per call; behavioral objectives and compatibility constraints are separate from accepted outcome metrics.

sampler.constraint_policy: Use hard implications + forced dimension propagation. Raise on unsatisfiable config, never silently relax.

joint_balancing.interpretation: targets exact in expectation for sampled proposals where constraints permit; accepted distribution may differ

behaviors.objective: Clarify goal boundaries, deliverables, and measurable acceptance criteria
Identify uncertain premises and prioritize risks using evidence
Choose actionable milestones and order them around constraints
Select appropriately sized planning effort relative to urgency and project scale
Negotiate scope, deadlines, quality and constraints rather than hiding conflicts
Distinguish new evidence that warrants a change of course from minor noise
Choose low-cost experiments when uncertainty blocks commitment
Split a broad objective into independently verifiable deliverables
Identify prerequisites, critical path and blocked branches
Recognize independent work versus necessary sequencing
Assign unambiguous responsibility and avoid duplicate ownership
Refine too-big or ambiguous tasks while preserving progress
Design handoff/acceptance contracts between dependent tasks
Choose agents by strengths, tools, cost and risk
Avoid both excessive delegation and unnecessary coordinator implementation
Dispatch independent tasks without conflicting assignments
Track staggered results without losing outstanding work
Merge results only after required dependencies are observed
Intervene when owners stall, conflict or cannot meet requirements
Send concise actionable requests and status communications
Allow valid work to continue without churn, duplicate dispatch or spam
Assemble bounded, relevant context packets for each specialist
Resume from partial project history without resetting progress
Retain reasons and evidence for decisions and changed constraints
Detect and quarantine stale or superseded information
Reconcile incompatible agent reports without unsupported certainty
Notify only affected agents with relevant state changes
Preserve essential project state under short context limits
Set appropriate tests, criteria and verification owners
Differentiate agent claims from verified observations
Localize defects, request bounded repair and retest
Determine whether repair, reassignment or full replanning is warranted
Diagnose ambiguous failures and prioritize consequential ones
Confirm all outstanding obligations before answering or closing
Close verified work; stop or escalate when further progress is unjustified
Update plans and dependents when the user changes the goal
Use the cheapest adequate agent without jeopardizing quality
Invest in reusable automation only when its expected value is positive
Shift limited time, tokens or money toward highest-value obligations
Allocate scarce execution capacity across critical-path tasks
Stop sunk-cost optimization when expected benefit no longer justifies it
Pay for quality where error costs dominate, economize elsewhere
Select reusable infrastructure based on uncertain recurrence

variants.scenario_condition: A critical requirement is unknown and taking action could irreversibly waste work.
variants.target_behavior: Ask a focused clarifying question and do not invent approval or requirements.

variants.scenario_condition: The uncertainty is low impact and a reversible default is available.
variants.target_behavior: State a bounded assumption and make useful progress.

variants.scenario_condition: A credible unverified issue would materially change the plan.
variants.target_behavior: Collect discriminating evidence before committing.

variants.scenario_condition: The remaining risk is minor and further investigation costs more than likely impact.
variants.target_behavior: Record the risk and continue without excessive investigation.

variants.scenario_condition: A high-impact, feasible precaution is justified by available evidence.
variants.target_behavior: Prioritize a proportionate mitigation.

variants.scenario_condition: An identified prerequisite gates several valuable dependent tasks.
variants.target_behavior: Prioritize the gating task and preserve useful parallel work.

variants.scenario_condition: A firm deadline makes a narrow deliverable more urgent than optional improvements.
variants.target_behavior: Prioritize the deliverable due soon.

variants.scenario_condition: No hard deadline or blocker dominates, but tasks differ sharply in expected benefit.
variants.target_behavior: Prioritize expected project value.

variants.scenario_condition: The task is narrow, reversible, and already sufficiently specified.
variants.target_behavior: Create only the coordination structure needed.

variants.scenario_condition: Several interdependent deliverables require explicit owners and milestones.
variants.target_behavior: Produce a bounded plan before dispatch.

variants.scenario_condition: A valid plan exists but newly observed constraints require localized updates.
variants.target_behavior: Revise only the affected plan components.

variants.scenario_condition: Reducing verification would create disproportionate downstream risk.
variants.target_behavior: Protect the quality-critical work and adjust less important scope.

variants.scenario_condition: A clear scope reduction can preserve the highest-value deliverable before a hard deadline.
variants.target_behavior: Negotiate or reduce optional scope without false completion.

variants.scenario_condition: A meaningful budget or scope change exceeds existing permission.
variants.target_behavior: Explain options and request the required approval.

variants.scenario_condition: A changed constraint affects only a bounded subset of tasks.
variants.target_behavior: Repair affected tasks and notify dependent owners; preserve valid work.

variants.scenario_condition: A foundational assumption is invalid and most milestones no longer serve the objective.
variants.target_behavior: Rebuild the plan with explicit migration of reusable work.

variants.scenario_condition: New information is noisy or immaterial and the original approach remains valid.
variants.target_behavior: Avoid disruptive replanning.

variants.scenario_condition: A cheap test can resolve a consequential uncertainty before costly commitment.
variants.target_behavior: Commission a small decisive experiment.

variants.scenario_condition: The uncertainty is too small to justify experiment overhead.
variants.target_behavior: Proceed with the main task while recording assumptions.

variants.scenario_condition: The objective spans genuinely separable deliverables with different completion criteria.
variants.target_behavior: Decompose into bounded outputs and owners.

variants.scenario_condition: The objective is small enough that fragmentation would add overhead.
variants.target_behavior: Keep the work compact and avoid artificial subtasks.

variants.scenario_condition: Multiple tasks have no unsatisfied data dependencies and enough capacity exists.
variants.target_behavior: Dispatch independent tasks concurrently.

variants.scenario_condition: Later tasks require observations or artifacts from earlier tasks.
variants.target_behavior: Sequence dependent work and wait for prerequisite evidence.

variants.scenario_condition: Some tasks are independent while others form a critical path.
variants.target_behavior: Run only independent branches concurrently.

variants.scenario_condition: Multiple eligible agents and overlapping task interests create duplicate-work risk.
variants.target_behavior: Assign one accountable owner per task with clear handoff rules.

variants.scenario_condition: The original owner is unavailable or demonstrably incapable of finishing a required task.
variants.target_behavior: Record a visible ownership transfer rather than silently duplicating the task.

variants.scenario_condition: The specialist needs a narrow, well-specified output and most historical notes are irrelevant.
variants.target_behavior: Pass concise task-specific constraints and acceptance conditions.

variants.scenario_condition: A specialist decision depends on prior findings, constraints, and dependency artifacts.
variants.target_behavior: Include relevant state and provenance without dumping unrelated history.

variants.scenario_condition: The original handoff is incomplete or stale but recoverable evidence exists.
variants.target_behavior: Rebuild the missing context before dependent execution.

variants.scenario_condition: A routine verifiable task fits a cheaper specialist with adequate tools.
variants.target_behavior: Select the economical agent and set appropriate verification.

variants.scenario_condition: Errors are expensive or the task requires rare expertise unavailable to cheap agents.
variants.target_behavior: Use a capable specialist and justify additional cost.

variants.scenario_condition: No available specialist meets the task constraints and inventing a capability would be unsafe.
variants.target_behavior: Explain the limitation and escalate, defer, or seek authorization.

variants.scenario_condition: The work requires substantial specialist execution that a suitable available agent can perform.
variants.target_behavior: Delegate with defined scope, owner and acceptance criteria.

variants.scenario_condition: The request is a trivial coordination decision; delegation costs more than it saves.
variants.target_behavior: Handle the small coordination step directly, not specialist implementation.

variants.scenario_condition: A large team would create communication overhead without increasing useful throughput.
variants.target_behavior: Use only the minimum justified resources.

variants.scenario_condition: A required observation is pending and no useful independent work can proceed.
variants.target_behavior: Wait without fabricating a result or spinning on duplicate calls.

variants.scenario_condition: A dependency is pending but a separate useful task is unblocked.
variants.target_behavior: Continue the independent work while tracking the pending result.

variants.scenario_condition: A genuine service-level deadline has elapsed and escalation is permitted.
variants.target_behavior: Request status or escalate without inventing completion.

variants.scenario_condition: The issue has a bounded owner and can be repaired within delegated authority.
variants.target_behavior: Repair or reassign locally and update relevant state.

variants.scenario_condition: The decision exceeds granted authority or changes a material project commitment.
variants.target_behavior: Present options with evidence and request permission.

variants.scenario_condition: A change materially affects some but not all participants.
variants.target_behavior: Notify affected owners with an actionable, concise update.

variants.scenario_condition: Internal progress is routine and no participant needs another message.
variants.target_behavior: Avoid noisy updates and continue useful work.

variants.scenario_condition: A milestone or significant risk requires a user-facing status summary.
variants.target_behavior: Give an accurate progress report with uncertainty and next actions.

variants.scenario_condition: A partially completed project has an incomplete, potentially inconsistent handoff.
variants.target_behavior: Identify completed, pending, blocked and unknown obligations before continuing.

variants.scenario_condition: A reliable checkpoint/ledger already establishes current state.
variants.target_behavior: Continue without repeating completed work.

variants.scenario_condition: Available claims disagree or are stale on a consequential matter.
variants.target_behavior: Request discriminating observations and preserve provenance.

variants.scenario_condition: Evidence is current, trustworthy and sufficient for the decision.
variants.target_behavior: Proceed without repeating unnecessary validation.

variants.scenario_condition: The needed result has not been observed or cannot be verified.
variants.target_behavior: Explicitly mark unknown; do not assert that external work occurred.

variants.scenario_condition: A significant decision depends on a superseded record with a newer authoritative version.
variants.target_behavior: Check the updated source and reconcile the decision with the current record.

variants.scenario_condition: A consequential deliverable has a high impact error mode and no sufficient independent evidence.
variants.target_behavior: Arrange appropriate independent verification.

variants.scenario_condition: Relevant automated acceptance checks already give adequate assurance for the risk.
variants.target_behavior: Use existing verified evidence, avoiding redundant reviews.

variants.scenario_condition: Only a narrow interface or changed component requires fresh tests.
variants.target_behavior: Verify the affected boundary and preserve valid prior results.

variants.scenario_condition: A localized defect is understood and the original owner remains capable.
variants.target_behavior: Request bounded repair with retest criteria.

variants.scenario_condition: The owner is unavailable, unqualified, or repeated repair attempts failed.
variants.target_behavior: Transfer a bounded assignment with complete context.

variants.scenario_condition: A basic assumption or integration design is invalid.
variants.target_behavior: Revise the affected work plan rather than repeating failed attempts.

variants.scenario_condition: Every required deliverable is observed, accepted, and has no unresolved gating obligation.
variants.target_behavior: Close with a concise verified handoff.

variants.scenario_condition: At least one required deliverable is missing, unobserved, or fails acceptance.
variants.target_behavior: Do not claim completion; pursue remaining work.

variants.scenario_condition: No authorized useful progress remains while an external dependency or decision is outstanding.
variants.target_behavior: Explain the blocker and pause or escalate accurately.

variants.scenario_condition: Repeated work and reliable reuse create positive expected net value after build and maintenance costs.
variants.target_behavior: Commission proportional reusable tooling.

variants.scenario_condition: A one-off or low-volume task makes automation overhead unjustified.
variants.target_behavior: Use an existing tool or bounded manual delegation.

variants.scenario_condition: Future demand and savings are too uncertain to justify an irreversible investment.
variants.target_behavior: Use reversible execution and revisit if volume appears.

domains.description: Software or open-source implementation and maintenance

lifecycle.description: A new or freshly authorized project needs an initial direction
A significant deviation, failure, or change requires attention
The project is approaching acceptance, handoff, or stopping decision

complexity.description: Multiple teams, complex dependencies and longer state

entry_state.description: No previous work; all obligations are new
Existing progress has a reliable checkpoint
Project starts mid-execution with only partial documented history

recurrence.description: Work is unlikely to be repeated

resource_posture.description: Resources are adequate for reasonable execution
Deadline and throughput are binding constraints
Compute or monetary budget is binding
Two valuable objectives compete for the same resources

dependency_pattern.description: Key tasks require sequential evidence or artifacts
Independent branches eventually converge on an integration
One gating path coexists with independent useful work

information_state.description: Required information is reliable and available
Some requirements or observations are incomplete
A document or decision has been superseded
Two sources disagree on an important fact
A needed external result has not arrived

tool_access.description: Some useful tools are unavailable or limited
Tools allow inspection but consequential mutation is restricted
External tools cannot currently be reached

agent_reliability.description: Available specialists are generally competent and truthful
Agent competence is not established and needs verification

user_competence.description: User needs jargon-free explanations and has uncertain technical assumptions
User understands common terminology and tradeoffs
User is knowledgeable and may challenge assumptions

user_patience.description: User values concise, fast progress and dislikes unnecessary ceremony
User accepts more planning when demonstrably worthwhile

user_involvement.description: User delegates routine decisions but requires consent on consequential changes
User can answer focused questions and review milestones
User replies intermittently, so reversible autonomous progress matters

user_tone.description: User challenges recommendations and wants explicit justifications
User is concerned about pressure, failure, or looming deadlines

team_posture.description: Two or three available specialist agents
Four to five agents with different strengths
Six to eight agents with limited attention and coordination cost

incident.description: No material failure is currently known
A delivered artifact fails a documented acceptance test
A specialist becomes unavailable or times out
A decision was based on obsolete assumptions
The user changes an important requirement
Resource consumption exceeds the current allowance
Some tasks have duplicate owners or no completed observation
Required input is indefinitely delayed or unavailable

episode_goal.description: Advance the project faithfully without requiring complete delivery
Complete all required work and verify it before closure
Transfer work with an accurate ledger and next actions
Stop and seek help when no authorized useful progress exists
Preserve resources when acting now would be harmful

execution_pattern.description: Window and tool events progress mostly sequentially
Several windows make useful interleaved progress
Agent responses arrive in different orders and require result-task binding
Some windows or agents wait while independent work continues

decision_difficulty.description: A familiar decision with clear evidence and few competing values
Several reasonable alternatives require comparing their implications
Important objectives conflict, evidence is incomplete or wrong actions compound
An unusual but realistic combination challenges default heuristics

stakes.description: Local and reversible mistakes have limited consequences
Errors consume meaningful time, money or quality
Errors could seriously damage project quality, cost or continuity

project_timescale.description: Work can largely be coordinated within one session
The project spans several working days
The project spans many milestones and handoffs

observation_source.description: External agent messages are the primary evidence stream
Tool call responses are the primary evidence stream
Persistent files, reports and records provide evidence
Agent messages, tool calls and project records must be reconciled

window_role_profile.description: Minimize distinct concurrent roles when extra windows add no value
Planning and decision reasoning are prominent
Concurrent task assignment, tool interactions and summaries matter
Maintain records and assess conflicting observations
Verification records and final deliverables dominate

phase_transition.description: Episode stays mainly within its starting lifecycle phase
A proposal turns into authorized delegation and execution
An observed setback forces a recovery episode
Active work transitions to verified delivery and closeout
A failure is contained and useful execution resumes
A late failure is corrected and the work is verified
A final check reveals an unresolved obligation and reopens work

episode_horizon.description: A compact decision with limited surrounding events
A focused coordination sequence with evidence and follow-ups
Multiple tasks, observations and decisions unfold
A lengthy stateful continuation with interrupted context

ambiguous_requirements.description: Requirements admit multiple materially different interpretations

parallel_assignments.description: Two or more independent tasks should be delegated concurrently

asynchronous_result.description: At least one result arrives after an intervening decision

stale_context.description: An important prior statement is out of date

failed_acceptance.description: An output is observed failing a check

changed_constraints.description: A user or resource constraint changes after work starts

external_approval.description: Progress is gated by consequential user authorization

expensive_model_tradeoff.description: Cheaper and expert agent options have materially different cost

automation_candidate.description: Recurring work makes an automation investment plausible

handoff_information_loss.description: A dependent agent lacks a needed result or rationale

deadline_shift.description: Priority ordering must account for an altered due date

resource_exhaustion.description: A budget or capacity limit is close to binding

untrusted_tool_output.description: An observation contains questionable or incomplete claims

out_of_order_completion.description: Tasks complete in a different order than dispatched

decision_requires_pushback.description: The user proposes a flawed plan and would benefit from concise critique

insufficient_evidence.description: One result is missing and must not be hallucinated

task_cancelled.description: A changed objective makes a previously valid task unnecessary

tool_call_failure.description: A real attempted tool interaction visibly fails

no_useful_work.description: Waiting or justified stopping is the appropriate next action

metrics_schema.unit: one generated definition; accepted trajectories reported only after explicit downstream acceptance
